mechanism_narrative: A sustained decline in the federal funds rate over the past three months indicates an accommodative monetary policy stance that lowers discount rates for equity valuation, driving positive S&P 500 forward returns over the next 20 trading days.
failure_condition: SPX 20-day returns are negative in more than 60% of periods where FEDFUNDS has declined over the past 3 months, or Rank IC over 3-year rolling windows remains below 0.03.

mechanism_narrative: When the federal funds rate exceeds 4.0% for two consecutive months, it signals restrictive monetary policy that increases cost of capital and reduces equity valuations, causing negative S&P 500 forward returns over the next 5 trading days.
failure_condition: SPX 5-day returns are positive in more than 60% of periods where FEDFUNDS has been above 4.0% for two consecutive months, or Rank IC over 3-year windows falls below 0.03.

mechanism_narrative: A simultaneous increase in the federal funds rate and decline in unemployment rate signals an overheating economy with tightening policy amid strong labor market, increasing recession risk and driving negative S&P 500 forward returns over 20 trading days.
failure_condition: SPX 20-day returns are positive in more than 60% of periods where FEDFUNDS rose and UNRATE fell simultaneously, or interaction term Rank IC over 3-year windows is below 0.03.

mechanism_narrative: In a high-unemployment regime (UNRATE > 5.0%), a decline in unemployment rate signals labor market strength that may precede recession due to policy tightening, causing negative S&P 500 forward returns over 60 trading days.
failure_condition: SPX 60-day returns are positive in more than 60% of periods where UNRATE > 5.0% and UNRATE declined, or Rank IC over 3-year windows is below 0.03.

mechanism_narrative: A sustained upward trend in non-farm payroll employment over the past three months indicates robust labor market conditions supporting consumer spending and corporate earnings, driving positive S&P 500 forward returns over 20 trading days.
failure_condition: SPX 20-day returns are negative in more than 60% of periods where PAYEMS trended upward for 3 months, or Rank IC over 3-year windows remains below 0.03.

mechanism_narrative: When housing starts fall below 1400.0 thousand units for two consecutive months, it signals weakening consumer demand and broader economic slowdown, causing negative S&P 500 forward returns over 5 trading days.
failure_condition: SPX 5-day returns are positive in more than 60% of periods where HOUST has been below 1400.0 for two consecutive months, or Rank IC over 3-year windows falls below 0.03.

mechanism_narrative: A simultaneous decline in housing starts and industrial production signals broad-based economic slowdown with weak consumer demand and reduced manufacturing output, increasing recession fears and driving negative S&P 500 forward returns over 20 trading days.
failure_condition: SPX 20-day returns are positive in more than 60% of periods where HOUST and INDPRO both declined simultaneously, or interaction term Rank IC over 3-year windows is below 0.03.

mechanism_narrative: In a slow-growth regime (GDPC1 quarterly growth < 1.5%), a decline in real personal consumption expenditure (RSAFS) signals deteriorating consumer demand, leading to negative S&P 500 forward returns over 60 trading days as recession risks increase.
failure_condition: SPX 60-day returns are positive in more than 60% of periods where GDPC1 growth < 1.5% and RSAFS declined, or Rank IC over 3-year windows remains below 0.03.
